name: Scripting Benchmark
description: Startup-sensitive snippets, sustained computation, and file/data workloads. Compare all participating languages with checked outputs and retained samples.

name: Website Generator Benchmark
description: From 100 to 10,000 pages: full builds, Nift incremental and targeted builds, elapsed time, and memory—with output equivalence and state boundaries attached.

name: Shell Benchmark
description: Startup and RC costs, native scripting, process scaling and mixed 100k-file tasks. Bash, Zsh, Fish, Nushell and Nift, with checked outputs and explicit native/Unix-tool boundaries.

name: Build Systems Benchmark
description: GNU Make, Ninja and Nift execute the same native graph. No-op and incremental scaling, generated inputs, compiler-heavy builds and tiny actions—with exact rebuilt sets and output hashes.

name: Task Runners Benchmark
description: Nift, Turbo and Nx execute controlled project workflows and tiny tasks. Exact execution sets, file invalidation, concurrency, targeting, failure recovery and local-state boundaries.

name: Template Engines Benchmark
description: Five engines assemble identical documents. Fresh invocation, preparation, reuse, loops, partials and memory, with exact byte checks and a candid practitioner assessment.

name: Concurrency Benchmark
description: Five runtimes solve equivalent concurrency problems: scheduling, waits, CPU scaling, bounded pools, queues, shared state, subprocesses and memory. Exact correctness and explicit model boundaries.
